answer.rationale: The objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, not a short-term account count. That immediately deprioritizes promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 is the one inherited record with a quantified downside (first-term renewals -12pp, price-sensitive buyer mix, explicitly marked unsuitable for repeat use). Matching a price attack would buy top-of-funnel numbers while importing exactly the cohort that churns, so the headline win would mask a value loss downstream. Referral incentive (memory_57) is real but works on established customers and does nothing for the two metrics actually degrading. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) is a pipeline-quality lever, not an activation/onboarding lever, and cannot absorb a one-week slot productively. That leaves the two levers pointed at the observed decay: onboarding shortening (memory_86) and in-product activation messaging (memory_91). Onboarding completion is down 4% and activation is down 6%, and onboarding completion is plausibly upstream of activation, so fixing the earlier step could recover both; that is why I lean simplify_onboarding. But I am choosing between two compressed summaries that both assert directional lift with no effect sizes, no durability window, and no holdout description, so I am spending both verification pulls on memory_86 and memory_91 to see which original record actually supports a causal, durable effect rather than a correlational read. I did not verify memory_31 because it is a distinct lever (signup fields, not onboarding length) and its claim of a durable first-week lift is the weaker input to this decision; if memory_86's source turns out thin, memory_31 becomes the fallback framing and I would drop to a guarded test instead. Key risk I am carrying forward and will instrument against: shortening onboarding can lift completion by removing steps that were doing qualification or setup work, producing a completion metric that rises while genuine time-to-value and downstream qualified revenue fall. So the experiment must be measured on activation and first-term retention of the affected cohort, not on completion rate alone, and I am running it as a standard experiment with a holdout rather than a broad rollout. My belief here is provisional and will be revised on what the two archived records actually show.
